# Zal

> Programmable payments on an Avalanche L1. Every party gets the same on-chain account, drawn as a canvas of nodes and edges, where it sets the rules for money in and out. Two canvases link as buyer and seller. The seller issues an invoice as an NFT; the buyer approves and pays it in one transaction that runs through both parties' rules; a funding pool can advance 80% to the seller as soon as the buyer approves (reverse factoring). v1 is live on testnet (Avalanche L1 on Fuji, chain id 102026) with testnet zUSDC only.

Headline: "Every money flow, one canvas." Category: programmable payments. Audience: individuals, teams and businesses. First segment: clubs, small teams and their suppliers.

Status legend used below: **live** = deployed and usable on the testnet L1 and in the sandbox; **planned** = designed, not built; **out of scope** = deliberately excluded from v1.

## Try it

- App: https://app.100-63-191-30.sslip.io
- Sandbox (no wallet, runs the real contract bytecode in the browser, with bots and a movable clock): https://app.100-63-191-30.sslip.io/app/canvas?sandbox=1
- Explorer: https://app.100-63-191-30.sslip.io/app/explorer
- REST API: https://api.100-63-191-30.sslip.io/v1
- Local: `docker compose up -d --build --wait` (postgres, anvil, deploy, indexer, web), then http://localhost:3100

## Problem

| Problem | Today |
|---|---|
| Manual operations | Splits, approvals and reconciliation done by hand |
| Fragmented tools | Bank, spreadsheet and invoice software, each apart |
| Broken settlement | Payments between parties wait and get re-confirmed |
| Trust dependence | Money rules live with whoever keeps the books |

A seller with an agreed invoice still waits until the due date for cash.

## Solution

1. Design: draw money in and out on a canvas (budgets, signatures, how income splits).
2. Connect: link counterparties, issue and approve invoices.
3. Execute: one transaction runs every party's rules.

## Platform pillars

| Pillar | Meaning | Where it is in code |
|---|---|---|
| Programmable Flows | Design any money flow | `CanvasAccount`: budgets, M-of-N policy, Split, schedules |
| Composable Finance | Combine any financial tool | Invoice NFT, ERC-4626 funding pool, ERC-4626 vault as plug-in legs |
| Counterparty Network | Connect every counterparty, one transaction | `RelationshipRegistry`, invite links, one-transaction settlement |
| On-chain Enforcement | Contracts enforce the rules | Every rule that moves or commits money is on-chain |

## Design principles

1. One canvas for everyone. Every party is the same `CanvasAccount` contract (ERC-1167 clone). No buyer or seller mode.
2. Roles belong to relationships, never accounts. A club is a seller to its sponsor and a buyer from its designer with the same canvas.
3. Nothing lands on another canvas without consent. One side proposes, the other accepts.
4. Chain state decides what the UI shows. Draft (local only), Pending/ghost (on-chain, awaiting the other side), Committed/solid.
5. The NFT holder gets paid. Payment goes to `ownerOf(invoiceId)`: the seller, or the pool once funded.
6. Settlement is one transaction: buyer, then the pool if funded, then the seller's Split.
7. Rounding favours the pool. Split remainders go to the last leg.
8. No oracles, no upgradeability, no arbitrary calls from accounts.

## Features (v1, all live unless marked)

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| Canvas | One per party; created in one transaction on wallet connect |
| Members | Solo or shared. Admin, Approver, Viewer. A wallet can belong to several canvases (canvas switcher, checked on-chain via `roleOf`) |
| Approval policy | M of N signatures above a single-signature allowance per rolling 24 h across the whole account; splitting a payment does not avoid it; member or policy change voids pending ops |
| Budget | Spending limit per 30-day period; invoice approval charges it |
| Counterparty | Propose by canvas address, or invite by EIP-712 signed link (7 days, single use) |
| Invoice | ERC-721. Issue, approve, reject, cancel, escrow, pay |
| Escrow | Buyer locks exactly face value; anyone may settle once due |
| One-transaction payment | Buyer → funding pool (if advanced) → seller's Split, atomically |
| Split | Up to 8 legs (Hold, Transfer, Vault) summing to 100%; a failing leg falls back to Hold and emits `LegFailed` instead of reverting settlement |
| Split visibility | Public or private in the Zal UI (on-chain data stays public) |
| Schedule | Pay an approved invoice at a set time, or a fixed transfer once or recurring (1–1,000 runs); run by a permissionless keeper |
| Funding pool | ERC-4626. Advance 80% of face on an approved invoice; fee fixed at advance; reserve paid to the seller's Split at payment |
| Liquidity provision | Any wallet deposits zUSDC, earns advance fees; withdrawals capped by idle cash |
| Vault | ERC-4626 for idle cash; yield simulated (rate TBD, deployed 0) |
| Child canvas | Group nodes into one level of sub-canvas; presentation only |
| Workspace | Inbox (6 notification kinds, realtime), Timeline, Overview charts, canvas switcher |
| Sandbox | Whole demo alone in the browser on the real bytecode |
| Onboarding | Gas faucet (0.05 ZAX, rate-limited per wallet and IP) and mint 1,000 testnet zUSDC |
| Stream | Not in v1 (shown disabled) |

## Reverse factoring, worked example (the demo)

Designer D sells to club C (3 members, 2-of-3 policy). LP L funds pool P.

1. D sets Split: 10% tax, 90% hold.
2. D proposes C as buyer; C accepts. Both canvases show the relationship.
3. D issues a 5,000 invoice due in 30 days (NFT minted to D).
4. c1 approves it against the "Events" budget; c2 confirms; C escrows 5,000.
5. L deposits 10,000 into P.
6. D requests an advance: receives 4,000 now; the NFT moves to P; the payee becomes P.
7. C pays 5,000 in one transaction: P keeps 4,000 + fee (≈ 50 at the deployed `annualFeeBps` 1521 over 30 days); the reserve goes through D's Split, 10% and 90%.

Credit safety: the pool advances only against a fully escrowed invoice, or a buyer the pool owner enrolled with a credit limit. A self-dealing pair with neither is refused.

## Architecture

- On-chain (authority): `ZalFactory`, `CanvasAccount` (clones), `RelationshipRegistry`, `ZalInvoice` (ERC-721), `ZalFundingPool` (ERC-4626), `ZalVault` (ERC-4626, simulated), `ZUSDC`. Solidity 0.8.25, cancun, OpenZeppelin 5, Foundry.
- Canvas pipeline, abstractly: Inflow → Policy → Route → Outflow. Modules (invoice, pool, vault, schedule) plug into stages. A relationship link carries one transaction from A's outflow to B's inflow.
- Triggers: a party, a counterparty, or time (keeper).
- Off-chain (presentation only): web app (Next.js 16, HeroUI v3, xyflow, wagmi, viem; tevm sandbox), indexer (Ponder + Hono `/v1` REST API, Postgres, SSE realtime, SIWE sign-in), keeper (gas-only wallet, calls `runSchedule`).
- Only presentation lives off-chain: node positions, child canvases, display names, read state, invites. Anything that moves or commits money is on-chain.
- The client treats the API as untrusted for money: transaction targets and signing data come from its own chain reads.

## Security model (highlights)

- `CanvasAccount.receivePayment` callable only by `ZalInvoice` or `ZalFundingPool` (AT-16).
- Gated selectors allow-listed with exact calldata lengths; the account never makes arbitrary calls.
- `policyNonce` voids pending ops when members or policy change (AT-13).
- Rolling 24 h allowance prevents splitting a spend into small ops (AT-26, AT-27).
- Invoice NFT moves only seller → pool while approved (AT-12); no third-party assignment.
- Malicious vault or transfer legs cannot block settlement (AT-15, AT-20).
- Transient reentrancy guards on every USDC-moving entry; 6-decimal virtual share offset against first-depositor inflation.
- Admins are fully trusted on their own canvas; the threshold protects spending operations.

## Verification

Specification-driven: 40+ requirements (`ZR-*`), 12 invariants (`INV-*`), 27 acceptance tests (`AT-*`), traced from PRD stories to test functions (every AT test name carries its ID).

| Suite | Result (15 Nov 2026) |
|---|---|
| Contracts: unit, acceptance, fuzz, invariants | 11 suites, 165 passed |
| Indexer | 73 passed |
| Keeper | 13 passed |
| Web (canvas model, API client, sandbox demo on real bytecode) | 260 passed |
| Mutation testing | 85 named mutants, each tagged with the INV or ZR it breaks |
| Contract sizes | All under 24,576 B |

Also: stack demo test (PRD demo on anvil through API and SSE), full reindex equality test, headless E2E for sandbox and live network.

## Why Avalanche

| Reason | For Zal | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Own Avalanche L1 | Own chain, own fees and gas token (ZAX), no shared congestion | Live on Fuji |
| EVM | Solidity, OpenZeppelin, Foundry; same bytecode in the browser sandbox | Live |
| Fast, final settlement | Finality in about a second, no reorgs; matters when one transaction runs several parties' rules | Live |
| Native interchain (ICM/ICTT) | Path to real USDC from C-Chain and cross-chain finance without third-party bridges | Planned |

## Network and deployment

- Network: Zalax Payroll Chain, Avalanche L1 on Fuji. Chain ID `102026`. Gas token ZAX. TxAllowList disabled (open chain).
- RPC: `https://rpc.100-63-191-30.sslip.io/ext/bc/L8z3EMtv6swD96pmVRsRLgYJR6iipDf8tSDe8vVnfqbHX7rxC/rpc`
- Deployed 15 Nov 2026, block 24.

| Contract | Address |
|---|---|
| ZalFactory | `0xb6fB0bAE55C3B10A52AbFB12a954F9AD7ce10013` |
| CanvasAccount (implementation) | `0xb67FF575307699dDACd58F581b894C9C316b1EF6` |
| RelationshipRegistry | `0x5FE372365723AAA13F59a790fB09CFC17914a191` |
| ZalInvoice | `0xf95A169Fd0A5190F3661FFd8bcdE45f229f4D972` |
| ZalFundingPool | `0xdfaE31B5d0B46595220788A81821f669f63CF11c` |
| ZalVault | `0x7fF89d37623f70987485deec28ACC7a38bd73F78` |
| ZUSDC | `0x443B9429EA87faAE61c3cCb6b10477D6993E1c30` |

Parameters: `advanceRateBps` 8000 (80%), `annualFeeBps` 1521 (proposed demo value), `vaultSimulatedApyBps` 0.

## Honest limits of v1

- Testnet only: zUSDC has no value; vault yield is simulated.
- On-chain data is public; "private" Split visibility is a UI rule, not privacy.
- Pool fees are recognised at repayment, not accrued (K-1); an unpaid funded invoice is not written down (K-2).
- Out of scope: streams, ending a relationship, buyer-created invoices, credit scoring, recourse and disputes, invoice resale, real money, KYC, fiat, mainnet, mobile.
- Planned: per-enterprise public and private credit pools (design only), bridged USDC via ICTT.
